# Linear Algebra, Live (Steppeschool)

> An interactive linear algebra course: eight lessons following the order of Gilbert Strang's Introduction to Linear Algebra, with live Python in the browser on every slide, worked examples and problems with full solutions. Applications in drones, IMUs and robot arms.

- Lessons 1 to 3 are free. The full course (all 8 lessons, members-only problems) is a one-time $20 with lifetime access: https://www.steppeschool.com/offers/57ZvEAFX/checkout
- Every lesson includes Steppe, an AI tutor that answers questions about the slide.
- Made by Steppeschool (https://www.steppeschool.com), embedded systems and robotics courses.

## Vectors, Linear Combinations and Matrix Multiplication

- [Vectors, Linear Combinations and Matrix Multiplication](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vectors-and-matrices/): Learn vectors, linear combinations, length and the dot product, matrix times vector by rows and by columns, and the column space, with interactive Python. Free lesson following Professor Strang.
- [Linear Combination of Vectors, Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vectors-and-matrices/linear-combinations/): What cv + dw really means, with an everyday picture, a worked example and Python you can run in your browser. Follows Strang §1.1.
- [Dot Product and Vector Length, Explained Simply](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vectors-and-matrices/lengths-and-dot-products/): What the dot product v · w means, how to compute it, how the length of a vector comes from it, and why a zero dot product means a right angle. Python in your browser. Strang §1.2.
- [Matrix-Vector Multiplication: Ax as a Combination of Columns](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vectors-and-matrices/matrix-vector-multiplication/): Why Ax is a mix of the columns of A, explained with a shopping basket, a worked example and live Python. Row way vs column way. Strang §1.3.
- [Column Space Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vectors-and-matrices/column-space/): The column space is everything Ax can reach. Learn it with a simple walking picture, rank, a worked example and Python you can run. Strang §1.3 and §3.1.
- [Lesson 1 Recap: Columns First](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vectors-and-matrices/recap/): The core ideas of Strang chapter 1 on one page: linear combinations, length and dot product, Ax by rows and by columns, and the column space.

## Gaussian Elimination and LU Decomposition

- [Gaussian Elimination and LU Decomposition](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/): Solve Ax = b: the row and column pictures, Gaussian elimination, pivots, elimination matrices, matrix multiplication and A = LU, with live Python in your browser. Free lesson.
- [Row Picture vs Column Picture of Ax = b](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/row-and-column-picture/): Two ways to see a linear system: lines crossing, or columns combining to make b. Interactive plot and Python in the browser. Strang §2.1.
- [Gaussian Elimination Method Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/gaussian-elimination/): How elimination solves two equations: subtract to remove an unknown, then back-substitute. A café puzzle, a worked example and live Python. Strang §2.2.
- [Pivots and Back Substitution: 3×3 Elimination Step by Step](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/pivots-and-back-substitution/): Clear one column at a time with the pivots, reach an upper triangular U, then solve from the bottom up. Worked 3×3 example with Python. Strang §2.2.
- [When Elimination Fails: Zero Pivots and Singular Systems](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/zero-pivots-and-singular-systems/): A zero pivot means swap rows or stop. See the three cases in the row picture: one solution, no solution, infinitely many. Strang §2.2.
- [Elimination Matrices: Row Operations as Matrix Multiplication](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/elimination-matrices/): Every elimination step is a matrix E. Multiplying by E subtracts a multiple of one row from another. Build E21 and E31 in Python. Strang §2.3.
- [Matrix Multiplication Explained: Row Times Column, Step by Step](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/matrix-multiplication/): How to multiply two matrices: each entry is a row times a column (a dot product), and each column of AB is A times a column of B. Worked examples, sizes, why AB is not BA, and Python. Strang §2.4.
- [LU Decomposition Method Explained: Why A = LU](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/lu-decomposition/): Elimination turns A into U, and the multipliers fill a lower triangular L so that A = LU. Factor once, solve many times. Python example. Strang §2.6.
- [Lesson 2 Recap: Elimination and A = LU](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/gaussian-elimination-and-lu/recap/): Lesson 2 in one page: row and column pictures, multipliers and pivots, back substitution, zero pivots and row exchanges, elimination matrices, matrix multiplication, and A = LU.

## Inverse Matrix, Transpose and Permutation Matrices

- [Inverse Matrix, Transpose and Permutation Matrices](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/): The inverse matrix, the 2x2 inverse formula, Gauss-Jordan, transposes, symmetric and permutation matrices, with interactive Python. Free lesson.
- [Inverse Matrix Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/inverse-matrix/): The inverse matrix undoes A: apply A, then its inverse, and every vector is back where it started. Worked examples, moving pictures and Python. Strang §2.5.
- [2×2 Inverse Matrix Formula and When It Fails](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/inverse-2x2-formula/): Swap the diagonal, flip the other signs, divide by ad − bc. What the determinant ad − bc tells you, and why 0 means no inverse. Worked examples and Python. Strang §2.5.
- [Inverse of a Product: Why (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/inverse-of-a-product/): To undo AB you undo A first, then B, so the order flips: (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹. Socks and shoes, worked 2×2 and 3×3 examples and live Python. Strang §2.5.
- [Gauss-Jordan Method: Find the Inverse of a Matrix](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/gauss-jordan/): Put A next to the identity and eliminate until A becomes I. The identity turns into the inverse. Worked 2×2 and 3×3 examples, with rref in Python. Strang §2.5.
- [Transpose and Symmetric Matrices Explained](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/transpose-and-symmetric-matrices/): The transpose swaps rows and columns. Why (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ, what a symmetric matrix is, and why AᵀA is always symmetric. Worked examples and Python. Strang §2.7.
- [Permutation Matrices: Reordering Rows](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/permutation-matrices/): Permutation matrices reorder the rows of a matrix. Why P⁻¹ = Pᵀ, and how PA = LU handles zero pivots, with worked 3×3 examples and Python. Strang §2.7.
- [Lesson 3 Recap: Inverses, Transposes and Permutations](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/inverse-transpose-permutation/recap/): Lesson 3 in one page: inverses, the 2×2 formula and the determinant ad − bc, the inverse of a product, Gauss-Jordan, transposes, symmetric matrices and permutation matrices.

## Vector Spaces, Null Space and the Four Subspaces

- [Vector Spaces, Null Space and the Four Subspaces](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/): Subspaces, the null space, rref and special solutions, the complete solution to Ax = b, basis, dimension and the four fundamental subspaces.
- [Vector Spaces and Subspaces Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/vector-spaces-and-subspaces/): A subspace is a set you cannot leave by adding and scaling: a line or plane through the origin. Examples, non-examples and live Python. Strang §3.1.
- [Null Space of a Matrix: How to Find It, Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/null-space/): The null space is every x with Ax = 0: inputs that produce no output. A walking picture, worked 2×2 and 3×3 examples and interactive Python. Strang §3.2.
- [Reduced Row Echelon Form, Pivot Columns and Special Solutions](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/rref-and-special-solutions/): Reduce A to R, spot the pivot and free columns, and build the special solutions that fill the null space. Worked 2×4 and 3×4 examples with Python. Strang §3.2.
- [The Complete Solution to Ax = b: Particular Plus Null Space](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/complete-solution/): Every solution of Ax = b is one particular solution plus any null space vector. See the solution line in an interactive plot and find it in Python. Strang §3.3.
- [Linear Independence, Basis and Dimension Explained](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/independence-basis-dimension/): Independent vectors, a basis and the dimension of a space, with a walking-directions picture, a 3D example and rank in Python. Strang §3.4.
- [The Four Fundamental Subspaces Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/four-fundamental-subspaces/): Row space, column space, null space and left null space: their dimensions and how they fit together, with an interactive picture. Strang §3.5.
- [Lesson 4 Recap: The Four Subspaces](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/vector-spaces-and-four-subspaces/recap/): Chapter 3 on one page: subspaces, the null space, special solutions, the complete solution to Ax = b, basis, dimension and the four subspaces.

## Orthogonality, Projections and the Least Squares Method

- [Orthogonality, Projections and the Least Squares Method](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/): Orthogonal subspaces, projection onto a line, projection matrices, least squares line fitting and Gram-Schmidt, with interactive Python.
- [Orthogonal Vectors and Subspaces Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/orthogonal-subspaces/): Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero. The row space is perpendicular to the null space. Examples and live Python. Strang §4.1.
- [Projection Onto a Line: Formula and Picture](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/projection-onto-a-line/): Project b onto the line through a: p = (aᵀb / aᵀa) a, the closest point, with the error perpendicular to a. Examples and Python. Strang §4.2.
- [Projection Matrix P = A(AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ Explained](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/projection-matrix/): The projection onto a line is Pb with P = aaᵀ/aᵀa. Onto the column space of A, P = A(AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ. Why P² = P, with examples and Python. Strang §4.2.
- [Least Squares Method and the Normal Equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/least-squares/): When Ax = b has no solution, least squares finds the best x̂ by solving AᵀAx̂ = Aᵀb. Why it works, worked examples and Python. Strang §4.3.
- [Least Squares Regression Line: Fitting a Line to Data](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/fitting-a-line/): Fit the best straight line C + Dt to noisy sensor data. Drag C and D to shrink the squared error, then solve the normal equations. Strang §4.3.
- [Orthonormal Basis and Orthogonal Matrices (QᵀQ = I)](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/orthonormal-bases/): Orthonormal vectors are perpendicular with length 1. In Q they give QᵀQ = I and Q⁻¹ = Qᵀ. Examples and Python. Strang §4.4.
- [Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization Process Step by Step (A = QR)](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/gram-schmidt/): Gram-Schmidt turns independent vectors into an orthonormal basis: subtract projections, divide by length, and get A = QR. Strang §4.4.
- [Lesson 5 Recap: Orthogonality, Projections and Least Squares](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/orthogonality-and-least-squares/recap/): Chapter 4 on one page: orthogonal subspaces, projections, least squares and the normal equations, line fitting, orthonormal bases, Gram-Schmidt.

## Determinants: Area, Properties, Cofactors and Cramer's Rule

- [Determinants: Area, Properties, Cofactors and Cramer's Rule](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/): What the determinant measures, its three rules, computing it from pivots or cofactors, Cramer's rule, the inverse formula and cross products.
- [Linear Transformations and Matrices: Rotation Matrix Intuition](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/linear-transformations/): See a matrix move the plane. Why the columns are where (1, 0) and (0, 1) land, how a rotation matrix is built, and what the determinant measures.
- [Reflection Matrix Challenge: Mirror the F](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/reflection-matrix/): Build the 2x2 matrix that mirrors the plane, and see why a reflection has determinant −1. An interactive linear algebra challenge in Python.
- [What Is a Determinant? Area and Volume Scale Factor](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/determinant-as-area/): The determinant says how much a matrix stretches area (2D) or volume (3D); its sign says whether space is flipped. Examples and Python. Strang §5.1.
- [Properties of Determinants: The Three Rules](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/properties-of-determinants/): Three rules define the determinant: det I = 1, a row swap flips the sign, det is linear in each row. All else follows. Examples and Python. Strang §5.1.
- [Determinant by Elimination: Product of the Pivots](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/determinant-from-pivots/): Compute any determinant by elimination: det A = ± (product of the pivots). Also det AB = det A det B and det Aᵀ = det A. Examples and Python. Strang §5.1.
- [Cofactor Expansion and the 3×3 Determinant Formula](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/cofactor-formula/): The big formula and cofactor expansion: a 3×3 determinant from 2×2 pieces with signs + − +. Worked examples and Python. Strang §5.2.
- [Cramer's Rule and the Inverse Matrix Formula](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/cramers-rule-and-inverse/): Cramer's rule solves Ax = b with ratios of determinants, and cofactors give A⁻¹ = Cᵀ / det A. When to use them and when not. Examples and Python. Strang §5.3.
- [Area of a Triangle, Volume and the Cross Product](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/area-volume-cross-product/): Determinants give a triangle's area from its corners, a box's volume from its edges, and the cross product u × v. Robotics examples and Python. Strang §5.3.
- [Lesson 6 Recap: Determinants](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/determinants/recap/): Lesson 6 on one page: how a matrix moves the plane, the mirror, the determinant as an area and volume factor, the three rules, pivots, cofactors, Cramer's rule, the inverse formula and cross products.

## Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors: Intuition and Diagonalization

- [Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors: Intuition and Diagonalization](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/): Eigenvalues and eigenvectors with live Python: det(A − λI) = 0, diagonalization, stability, Markov steady states, symmetric and positive definite matrices.
- [Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors Explained Visually: Ax = λx](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/eigenvectors/): An eigenvector is a direction that a matrix only stretches, never turns: Ax = λx. Find one by dragging an arrow, with examples and Python. Strang §6.1.
- [How to Find Eigenvalues: det(A − λI) = 0](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/finding-eigenvalues/): Find eigenvalues by solving det(A − λI) = 0, then eigenvectors from the null space of A − λI. Trace and determinant checks, examples and Python. Strang §6.1.
- [Diagonalizing a Matrix: A = XΛX⁻¹ and Matrix Powers](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/diagonalization/): With enough eigenvectors, A = XΛX⁻¹: eigenvectors in X, eigenvalues on the diagonal of Λ. Then powers are easy, Aᵏ = XΛᵏX⁻¹. Examples and Python. Strang §6.2.
- [Eigenvalues, Stability and Markov Matrices (Steady State)](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/powers-and-stability/): Repeating A makes parts grow or decay by their eigenvalues. Markov matrices settle to a steady state, the eigenvector for λ = 1. Python examples. Strang §6.2.
- [Symmetric Matrices: Real Eigenvalues and Orthogonal Eigenvectors](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/symmetric-matrices/): A symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and perpendicular eigenvectors, so A = QΛQᵀ with Q orthogonal: the spectral theorem. Examples and Python. Strang §6.4.
- [Positive Definite Matrices: Bowls, Saddles and Eigenvalues](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/positive-definite-matrices/): A symmetric matrix is positive definite when all its eigenvalues are positive, or xᵀAx > 0 for x ≠ 0: a bowl, not a saddle. Python examples. Strang §6.5.
- [Lesson 7 Recap: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors/recap/): Chapter 6 on one page: Ax = λx, det(A − λI) = 0, A = XΛX⁻¹, powers and stability, Markov steady states, symmetric and positive definite matrices.

## Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and PCA, Visually

- [Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and PCA, Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/): The SVD with live Python: every matrix as turn, stretch, turn, singular values, rank-one pieces, image compression, PCA and the pseudoinverse.
- [Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) Explained Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/svd-geometry/): The SVD says every matrix turns, stretches along perpendicular axes, then turns again: A = UΣVᵀ. The unit circle becomes an ellipse. Strang §7.4.
- [How to Find Singular Values: Eigenvalues of AᵀA](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/singular-values/): Singular values are square roots of the eigenvalues of AᵀA; its eigenvectors are the v's, and u = Av/σ. Worked examples and Python. Strang §7.2.
- [SVD as a Sum of Rank-One Matrices: A = σ₁u₁v₁ᵀ + σ₂u₂v₂ᵀ](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/svd-rank-one-pieces/): The SVD writes any matrix as a sum of simple rank-one pieces σuvᵀ, ordered from most to least important. Worked examples and Python. Strang §7.2.
- [Image Compression with the SVD (Low-Rank Approximation)](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/image-compression/): A grey image is a matrix. Keep only its largest singular values and the picture survives with far fewer numbers. Interactive Python example. Strang §7.1.
- [Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with the SVD, Visually](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/principal-component-analysis/): PCA finds the direction where data spreads most: center the data, take the first direction from the SVD. Interactive example with noisy robot positions. Strang §7.3.
- [Pseudoinverse and Condition Number from the SVD](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/pseudoinverse-and-condition-number/): The pseudoinverse A⁺ = VΣ⁺Uᵀ gives the best least-squares answer for any matrix, and σ₁/σₙ measures sensitivity. Python examples. Strang §7.4.
- [Lesson 8 Recap: The SVD and PCA](https://linearalgebra.steppeschool.com/svd-and-pca/recap/): Chapter 7 on one page: A = UΣVᵀ as turn-stretch-turn, singular values from AᵀA, rank-one pieces, image compression, PCA and the pseudoinverse.
